name: José del R. Millán
school: The University of Texas at Austin
title: Professor; Linda Steen Norris & Lee Norris Endowed Chair in Neuroengineering; Director of Texas Robotics
department: Electrical and Computer Engineering; Neurology; Biomedical Engineering by courtesy
fitReason: Direct AI/HRI fit in geometry-aware classification, neural-signal distribution shift and intention-gated robot assistance. A decoding/robustness or existing-data contribution could be scoped more narrowly than a clinical intervention, but that project has not been offered.

physicalEvidence.summary: The complete March 2026 ICRA manuscript verifies a Riemannian minimum-distance-to-mean EEG classifier gating a real Harmony SHR upper-limb exoskeleton. Eight healthy participants completed two online sessions; start/stop detections enabled or removed assistance through UDP while the robot retained its dynamics compensation and preprogrammed reach controller. Thus learned intent gates real physical execution, rather than directly generating arbitrary arm trajectories. The later fixation-based recentering improvement was evaluated pseudo-online on recorded data; fully online validation of that improvement and patient testing remain future work.

shortVisit.summary: The current CNBI homepage and team describe ongoing research and local students. A Visiting Students & Professors section identifies a visiting professor from Mexico, but does not invite external master’s students or provide short-term summer terms. No current eight-week opportunity, funding or remote arrangement was established.

scoreReasons.physical: 25/25: complete 2026 primary methods show trained EEG intent classifiers controlling real Harmony assistance with eight healthy users.

name: Jose Luis Contreras-Vidal
title: Hugh Roy and Lillie Cranz Cullen Distinguished Professor; Director, NSF IUCRC BRAIN Center
department: Electrical and Computer Engineering; IUCRC BRAIN Center
fitReason: Substantive AI methods include trainable neural denoising, spatial/time-frequency feature extraction and recurrent gait-state decoding, tied to physical exoskeleton control. The work is specialized biomedical robotics; simulation, signal processing or existing-data evaluation may be more realistic to scope than participant-facing work.

physicalEvidence.summary: The full August 2026 pilot deploys a neural feature-extraction block plus PolyTVL/LSTM gait decoder on an actual 10-actuator Rex lower-limb exoskeleton. A Python control system triggers steps from EEG predictions; one healthy participant completed five open-loop and five mixed open/closed-loop sessions. Rex-assisted initiation succeeded in 55.3% of trials, with 18.2% false positives. Mean inference including preprocessing was 70.5 ms, while valid end-to-end initiation latency was about 1.04 seconds. This is physical learned control, but remains a single-subject feasibility study, not demonstrated clinical effectiveness or broadly reliable autonomous walking.

shortVisit.summary: The BRAIN Center careers page says opportunity information is forthcoming. Its linked NSAP post-baccalaureate program is an explicit 10-week full-time program for May 26–July 31, 2026, restricted to US citizens/permanent residents. It is not an eight-week summer 2027 external-student invitation; older REU/undergraduate programs are not treated as master’s eligibility.

scoreReasons.fit: 37/40: substantial neural sequence modeling, trainable denoising and embodied assistance; narrower biomedical specialization than general-purpose robot learning.
scoreReasons.physical: 25/25: complete current primary methods demonstrate the learned decoder actuating a named real exoskeleton; single-user scale and modest performance retained.
scoreReasons.shortVisit: 0/20: no applicable current external-master visit invitation; the advertised 2026 NSAP program has separate duration and citizenship restrictions.
